flags.reason: optimizer.zero_grad() is called after backward() and immediately before optimizer.step(), erasing every gradient so training never updates parameters.
The module unconditionally imports models.resnet and models.clip, but neither file exists in the repository, so importing the main model fails before any architecture can run.
Most advertised readouts (including the default streams_inc) set rois_ind to an int and then iterate over it, causing an immediate TypeError; only list-valued voxels/rois_all pass this point.
The regression evaluation concatenates test features and test fMRI targets into its fitting data and then predicts/evaluates that same test set, directly leaking test labels.
The multi-model wrapper loads test fMRI ground truth and uses test-set correlations to compute per-vertex layer weights, making the ensemble's test evaluation circular.

The default 'transformer' decoder has no cross-attention: it convolves the spatial token sequence, averages it globally, and adds that same vector to every query, contradicting the README's core attention-routing mechanism.

Saved checkpoints deliberately remove all backbone_model keys, but both resume and wrapper loading use strict load_state_dict(), so checkpoints produced by this code cannot be loaded by its own loaders.
The dinov2 path replaces xs with a string-keyed dict and then indexes it with the integer enc_output_layer, producing a KeyError on every non-intermediate forward pass.
Resume accesses args.eval even though the parser defines args.evaluate, so every --resume invocation raises AttributeError.
Checkpoint saving omits optimizer and train_params, yet the resume branch initializes optimizer/scheduler/start_epoch only when those fields exist, leaving them unbound for checkpoints written here.
Attention extraction hooks decoder.layers[*].multihead_attn, but the current default decoder has no such attribute, so the supplied attention-map API crashes.
The advertised nsd_gen dataset branch calls undefined nsd_dataset_avg and also never constructs the validation/test loaders and ROI masks required later.
Category-specific criterion paths reference undefined lh_rois and rh_rois variables, so those readouts cannot compute a loss even if ROI setup is fixed.
The model is moved with unconditional .cuda() despite selecting a CPU device when CUDA is unavailable, making the claimed CPU fallback unusable.
When callers provide results_dir, the constructor never assigns self.results_dir, so the next model-path construction raises AttributeError.
Train/validation indices are shuffled from an unseeded global RNG on every run (the seed lines are commented out), so run IDs do not define reproducible or matched evaluation splits.

The architecture named dinov2_q actually instantiates a pretrained ConvNeXt-Tiny and ignores enc_output_layer, invalidating the repository's claimed DINO-Q backbone and its comparisons across backbone layers.

Hard-coded 31/11-token map sizes are incompatible with the actual ConvNeXt feature-grid sizes, causing spatial_feature matrix multiplications and linear readout dimensions to mismatch for the default backbone.
The saved-feature path creates a 1280-channel DINO-plus-CLIP map (and always loads both feature sets) but the model still feeds it through an image backbone expecting three-channel images.
--evaluate is parsed and documented as evaluation-only but is never checked, so using it still enters the full training loop.
